questions.q: What are the two equations that make up a general state-space model?
options: A mean equation and a variance equation
A state equation describing how the unobserved latent state evolves, and a measurement equation describing how that state generates noisy observed data
An ARCH equation and a GARCH equation
A trend equation and a seasonal equation
questions.explain: State-space models split the system into a state equation (state_t = T*state_(t-1) + w_t) and a measurement equation (obs_t = H_t*state_t + v_t).

questions.q: Under what conditions does the Kalman filter compute the exact optimal (minimum mean-squared-error) estimate of the latent state?
options: Only when the data has no noise at all
When both the state and measurement equations are linear and the noise terms are Gaussian
Only when the state is directly observed
Only when using more than 1,000 observations
questions.explain: In the linear-Gaussian case, the Kalman filter's recursive predict-update cycle is provably the optimal linear estimator of the latent state given all observations so far.

questions.q: How does the general state-space framework relate to Lesson 19's stochastic volatility model?
options: They are unrelated frameworks

Stochastic volatility is a state-space model with log-volatility as the latent state, but its measurement equation is nonlinear, which is why it typically needs a particle filter instead of the plain Kalman filter
Stochastic volatility models never have a latent state
The Kalman filter is only used for stochastic volatility models
questions.explain: SV models fit the state-space template with sigma_t as a latent state, but because r_t = sigma_t*z_t is nonlinear in the state, the plain linear Kalman filter doesn't directly apply, which is why SV estimation leans on particle filters or MCMC.

questions.q: In the worked example estimating a time-varying hedge ratio, how did the Kalman filter's accuracy compare to a 30-day rolling-OLS benchmark?
options: The rolling-OLS benchmark was more accurate (lower RMSE)
They performed identically
The Kalman filter had a lower RMSE (0.1094) than the 30-day rolling-OLS benchmark (0.1527), tracking the drifting true beta more accurately
Neither method could track the true beta at all
questions.explain: The Kalman filter's RMSE of 0.1094 against the true drifting beta was noticeably lower than the rolling-OLS benchmark's RMSE of 0.1527.

questions.q: In the time-varying hedge ratio example, what role does x_t (the other asset's return) play in the state-space formulation?
options: It is the latent state itself
It is the time-varying observation matrix H_t, mapping the latent beta into the observed y_t
It is pure noise with no modeling role
It is the transition matrix T
questions.explain: The measurement equation y_t = x_t * beta_t + v_t uses x_t as the time-varying H_t that maps the latent state (beta_t) into the observed measurement (y_t).
